newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu must demand he be charged - MP.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu must demand he be charged - MP.

text.p: The head of Israel's parliament law committee said on Thursday Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu should take leave and demand fraud and breach of trust charges recommended by police be filed against him.

Shaul Yahalom, a member of key government coalition member the National Religious Party (NRP), said that was the only way to bring an influence-peddling scandal to a quick end and prevent the political opposition from gaining advantage from it.

"If the prime minister would respond to my proposal...he would turn today to the attorney general and tell him that he was turning to him, agrees, requests, perhaps even demands... that he file a charge sheet against him," Yahalom said.
"In parallel, he should turn to the president of the High Court and request that the trial be conducted ... very quickly.

"This month the prime minister should take leave -- not suspend himself, not resign -- take leave. The law permits leave, to go on leave for up to three months ... In my opinion it's possible to finish everything in a month," he told Israel Radio.
Yahalom said Netanyahu could appoint a minister of his choice to act as prime minister during the trial.
Netanyahu spokesman Shai Bazak earlier on Thursday rejected calls for the prime minister's resignation.
"The prime minister has no intention of going now to elections or to resign or to suspend himself," Bazak told Israel Radio. "The prime minister is confident in his innocence. We are all sure of it."
Police said on Wednesday Netanyahu should be charged with fraud and breach of trust in an influence-peddling scandal. They said the recommendation was based on one witness's testimony.
The news dealt a crippling although not necessarily fatal political blow to the right-wing leader, analysts said.
Israel's state prosecutor can ignore the recommendation to put Netanyahu on trial for his short-lived appointment of political crony Roni Bar-On as attorney general in January.

Yahalom, whose party champions Jewish settlement of occupied Arab lands, said if no charges were filed against Netanyahu the main opposition Labour party would not let the matter rest but keep it alive for months with appeals to the High Court and other manoeuvres.
